subject: business-studies
promptStrong: Give me a challenging GCSE exam-style question on AQA Business marketing (market research, segmentation, the marketing mix, product life cycle and pricing), then mark my answer against the spec.
promptWeak: Explain an AQA GCSE Business marketing idea for GCSE Business simply, with an example and the most common mistake.
learningObjectives: Market segmentation by age, gender, location and income
Purpose of market research and primary vs secondary methods
Qualitative vs quantitative research and market size and share
The marketing mix (4Ps) and how the elements work together
The product life cycle and extension strategies
Pricing methods and factors influencing price
Promotional methods and the promotional mix
Place: channels of distribution, e-commerce and m-commerce

questions.q: Why is identifying and satisfying customer needs important to a business?
options: It means the business no longer has any competitors
It guarantees the business will never make a loss
It removes the need to do any market research
It helps the business provide products customers will buy and select the correct marketing mix
questions.explain: Understanding customer needs helps a business make products people will buy, choose the right marketing mix, increase sales and stay competitive. It does not guarantee profit or remove competition.

questions.lo: Market segmentation by age, gender, location and income
questions.q: Dividing a market into groups of customers with similar characteristics such as age or income is known as:
questions.explain: Market segmentation splits a market into groups sharing characteristics (age, gender, location, income) so a business can target them. Market research gathers data, and the marketing mix is the 4Ps.

questions.lo: Market segmentation by age, gender, location and income
questions.q: A company sells luxury watches costing thousands of pounds. Which segmentation base is MOST relevant when targeting its customers?
questions.explain: High-priced luxury goods are aimed at customers with high income, so income is the key segmentation base here. Age of packaging is not a segmentation base at all.

questions.lo: Purpose of market research and primary vs secondary methods
questions.q: Which of the following is an example of PRIMARY market research?
options: Looking at data from a competitor's website
Using figures from an existing market research report
Carrying out a questionnaire with customers
questions.explain: Primary research is first-hand data collected for a specific purpose, such as a questionnaire, survey, interview or focus group. Government reports, competitor websites and existing reports are secondary sources.

questions.lo: Purpose of market research and primary vs secondary methods
questions.q: What is a drawback of secondary market research compared with primary research?
options: It is always more expensive to collect
It always takes longer to obtain
The data may be out of date or not specific to the business's exact needs
It can only be gathered face-to-face
questions.explain: Secondary data already exists, so it is cheaper and quicker, but it may be outdated or not tailored to the business's specific question. Primary research is usually the more costly and time-consuming method.

questions.lo: Qualitative vs quantitative research and market size and share
questions.q: Which of the following best describes QUALITATIVE market research?
options: The total value of a market
Data about opinions, feelings and reasons behind customer behaviour
The percentage of a market held by one business
Numerical data such as how many people bought a product
questions.explain: Qualitative research gathers opinions, feelings and reasons (the 'why'), often from focus groups or interviews. Numerical 'how many' data is quantitative; the last two options describe market size and market share.

questions.lo: Qualitative vs quantitative research and market size and share
questions.q: A market is worth 5,000,000 pounds in sales per year and one firm sells 1,000,000 pounds of that. What is the firm's market share?
questions.explain: Market share = (firm's sales / total market sales) x 100 = (1,000,000 / 5,000,000) x 100 = 20%. Market size is the total value (5,000,000 pounds).

questions.lo: The marketing mix (4Ps) and how the elements work together
questions.q: Which of the following are the four elements of the marketing mix (the 4Ps)?
questions.explain: The 4Ps of the marketing mix are Product, Price, Place and Promotion. Profit, People and Process are not part of the AQA GCSE 4Ps.

questions.lo: The marketing mix (4Ps) and how the elements work together
questions.q: A firm launches a premium chocolate bar. To keep the mix consistent, which combination fits a premium product best?
options: High price, high-quality packaging and upmarket retailers
Low price and no promotion at all
High price sold only through a market stall
Low price, cheap packaging and discount-store distribution
questions.explain: The 4Ps must work together. A premium product needs a matching high price, quality packaging and upmarket distribution so the whole mix signals quality. Low prices and cheap outlets would contradict the premium image.

questions.q: What is a unique selling point (USP)?
options: A feature that makes a product stand out from its competitors
The location where a product is sold
The total number of products sold
The lowest price in the market
questions.explain: A USP is a feature or benefit that makes a product different from and more attractive than rivals, helping it stand out in a competitive market. It is not simply a low price or a sales figure.

questions.lo: The product life cycle and extension strategies
questions.q: Which of these lists the main stages of the product life cycle in the correct order?
questions.explain: After research and development, a product goes through introduction, then growth, then maturity, and finally decline. Sales rise through growth, peak at maturity, then fall in decline.

questions.lo: The product life cycle and extension strategies
questions.q: Sales of a product have started to fall. Which of the following is an EXTENSION strategy the business could use?
options: Adding new features or updating the packaging to boost sales
Raising the price to reduce demand
questions.explain: Extension strategies aim to prolong the maturity stage and delay decline, e.g. adding features, updating packaging, targeting a new market, advertising or reducing price. Withdrawing the product or cutting advertising would speed up decline.

questions.lo: Pricing methods and factors influencing price
questions.q: A business sets a HIGH initial price for a brand-new, innovative product to earn maximum revenue from early adopters. Which pricing method is this?
questions.explain: Price skimming charges a high price when a product is new and has little competition, then lowers it over time. Penetration pricing does the opposite by setting a low price to gain market share quickly.

questions.lo: Pricing methods and factors influencing price
questions.q: A new supermarket wants to win customers fast by setting prices below rivals when it enters the market. Which pricing method fits best?
questions.explain: Penetration pricing sets a deliberately low price on entry to attract customers and gain market share quickly. Skimming sets a high launch price, which would not help win price-sensitive shoppers.

questions.lo: Pricing methods and factors influencing price
questions.q: According to the basic relationship between price and demand, if a business raises its price, demand for the product is likely to:
questions.explain: Under the normal relationship, as price rises demand tends to fall, and as price falls demand tends to rise. Demand rarely stays exactly the same or instantly drops to zero.

questions.lo: Promotional methods and the promotional mix
questions.q: Which of the following is an example of a SALES PROMOTION?
options: A 'buy one get one free' offer
A press release to a newspaper
questions.explain: Sales promotions are short-term incentives to buy, such as BOGOF offers, free gifts, coupons and competitions. A TV advert is advertising, a press release is PR, and sponsoring a team is sponsorship.

questions.lo: Promotional methods and the promotional mix
questions.q: A small business with a very limited budget wants to promote a new product to a young, local audience. Which promotional method is likely to be MOST cost-effective?
questions.explain: Social media is low-cost and can precisely target a young, local audience, making it cost-effective for a small budget. National TV, national press and nationwide billboards are expensive and poorly targeted for this business.

questions.lo: Place: channels of distribution, e-commerce and m-commerce
questions.q: In the marketing mix, which of the following best describes 'place'?
options: The methods used to advertise the product
The features and design of the product
How and where products are made available to customers
The amount a business charges for a product
questions.explain: Place refers to the channels of distribution used to get products to customers, e.g. retailers, wholesalers, telesales or online. Charging is price, features are product and advertising is promotion.

questions.lo: Place: channels of distribution, e-commerce and m-commerce
questions.q: A UK craft business starts selling through its own website worldwide. Which benefit of e-commerce does this best illustrate?
options: It extends the reach of the business to include international markets
It removes all delivery and postage costs
It guarantees higher prices than high-street shops
It means the business no longer needs any stock
questions.explain: E-commerce lets a business sell online and reach customers far beyond its local area, including international markets, extending its reach. It does not remove delivery costs, remove the need for stock, or guarantee higher prices.
